title: Outstanding
query:
SELECT SUM(balance_aud) AS outstanding, COUNT(*) AS open_invoices, COUNT(DISTINCT client) AS clients
FROM invoices
WHERE balance_aud > 0
notes: Everything still owed, due or not. First tile because it is the number nearest the outcome: cash not yet in the bank.

title: Overdue
query:
SELECT SUM(balance_aud) AS overdue, COUNT(*) AS overdue_invoices,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM(balance_aud) / (SELECT SUM(balance_aud) FROM invoices WHERE balance_aud > 0), 1) AS pct_of_outstanding
FROM invoices
WHERE balance_aud > 0 AND days_past_due > 0
notes: The part of outstanding that is past its due date. Tone is bad whenever it is above zero.

title: Collected this month
query:
WITH m AS (SELECT MAX(date) AS asof FROM bank_transactions)
SELECT
  (SELECT SUM(credit_in) FROM bank_transactions, m
    WHERE date >= date(m.asof, 'start of month')) AS collected,
  (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(credit_in), 0) FROM bank_transactions, m
    WHERE date >= date(m.asof, 'start of month', '-1 month') AND date <= date(m.asof, '-1 month')) AS same_days_last_month,
  (SELECT SUM(credit_in) FROM bank_transactions, m
    WHERE date >= date(m.asof, 'start of month'))
  - (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(credit_in), 0) FROM bank_transactions, m
    WHERE date >= date(m.asof, 'start of month', '-1 month') AND date <= date(m.asof, '-1 month')) AS vs_last_month,
  (SELECT CAST(strftime('%d', asof) AS INTEGER) FROM m) AS days_in

delta.label: vs first {days_in} days of last month

notes: Month to date, anchored on the latest bank row so it works on a static file. The comparison is like for like: the same number of days of the month before, never a part month against a full one. On live data swap MAX(date) for date('now').

title: Average days to pay
query:
WITH pay AS (
  SELECT i.client, i.invoice_no, i.issue_date, i.due_date, b.date AS paid_date, b.credit_in AS paid,
         julianday(b.date) - julianday(i.issue_date) AS days_to_pay,
         julianday(b.date) - julianday(i.due_date)   AS days_late
  FROM bank_transactions b
  JOIN invoices i ON i.invoice_no = substr(b.description, instr(b.description, 'INV-'))
  WHERE b.credit_in IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT ROUND(AVG(days_to_pay), 1) AS avg_days_to_pay,
       ROUND(AVG(days_late), 1)   AS avg_days_late,
       COUNT(*)                   AS payments
FROM pay

chart.detail: {avg_days_late} days past due on 14-day terms · {payments} payments

notes: Issue date to the bank credit that references the invoice, averaged over every payment. Terms are 14 days on every invoice in the file, so anything above 14 is lateness.

title: Open tasks
query:
SELECT SUM(status <> 'done') AS open_tasks, SUM(status = 'blocked') AS blocked, SUM(status = 'in_progress') AS in_progress
FROM tasks
notes: Everything not done. Blocked is called out because it is the only status that needs a human.

title: Agent success rate
query:
SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(status = 'done') / SUM(status IN ('done', 'blocked')), 1) AS success_pct,
       SUM(status = 'done') AS done, SUM(status = 'blocked') AS blocked
FROM tasks
notes: The tasks table has no outcome column, so success is defined here as done ÷ (done + blocked): of the tasks that reached an end state or a wall, the share that finished. Change the definition in this one query if Ogdoad records run outcomes.

title: What is owed, by age
query:
WITH b(ageing_bucket, ord) AS (VALUES ('current', 0), ('1-30', 1), ('31-60', 2), ('61-90', 3), ('90+', 4))
SELECT b.ageing_bucket, b.ord,
       COALESCE(SUM(i.balance_aud), 0) AS owed,
       COUNT(i.invoice_no)             AS invoices
FROM b
LEFT JOIN invoices i ON i.ageing_bucket = b.ageing_bucket AND i.balance_aud > 0
GROUP BY b.ageing_bucket, b.ord
ORDER BY b.ord
notes: Five fixed buckets from a VALUES spine, so an empty bucket (61-90 today) still shows as a gap instead of vanishing. Colour is an ordered ramp from neutral to bad. Look for money piling up at the right-hand end.

title: Who owes what, by age
query:
SELECT client,
       SUM(CASE WHEN ageing_bucket = 'current' THEN balance_aud ELSE 0 END) AS not_due,
       SUM(CASE WHEN ageing_bucket = '1-30'    THEN balance_aud ELSE 0 END) AS d1_30,
       SUM(CASE WHEN ageing_bucket = '31-60'   THEN balance_aud ELSE 0 END) AS d31_60,
       SUM(CASE WHEN ageing_bucket = '61-90'   THEN balance_aud ELSE 0 END) AS d61_90,
       SUM(CASE WHEN ageing_bucket = '90+'     THEN balance_aud ELSE 0 END) AS d90_plus,
       SUM(balance_aud) AS owed
FROM invoices
WHERE balance_aud > 0
GROUP BY client
ORDER BY owed DESC
notes: One row per client, pivoted wide in SQL so each bucket is a plain series with its own encode. Sorted by total owed. One client carrying most of the bar length is the thing to notice.

title: Cash flow by month
query:
SELECT substr('JanFebMarAprMayJunJulAugSepOctNovDec', (CAST(strftime('%m', date) AS INTEGER) - 1) * 3 + 1, 3) || ' ' || substr(strftime('%Y', date), 3, 2)
         || CASE WHEN strftime('%m', date) = '07' OR strftime('%Y-%m', date) = (SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', MIN(date)) FROM bank_transactions)
                 THEN char(10) || 'FY' || substr(strftime('%Y', date, '+6 months'), 3, 2) ELSE '' END AS month,
       strftime('%Y-%m', date) AS ym,
       'FY' || substr(strftime('%Y', date, '+6 months'), 3, 2) AS fy,
       SUM(COALESCE(credit_in, 0))                                AS money_in,
       -SUM(COALESCE(debit_out, 0))                               AS money_out,
       SUM(COALESCE(credit_in, 0)) - SUM(COALESCE(debit_out, 0)) AS net
FROM bank_transactions
GROUP BY strftime('%Y-%m', date)
ORDER BY ym
notes: In above the line, out below it, net as a line on the same A$ axis. Each July label carries its financial-year tag (FY27 starts 1 July 2026), written by SQL so no formatter function is needed. The quarterly dips in net are BAS and super. The last month is a part month.

title: Net cash, this financial year vs last
query:
WITH m AS (
  SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', date) AS ym,
         CAST(strftime('%Y', date, '+6 months') AS INTEGER)  AS fy,
         (CAST(strftime('%m', date) AS INTEGER) + 5) % 12    AS fy_month_idx,
         SUM(COALESCE(credit_in, 0)) - SUM(COALESCE(debit_out, 0)) AS net
  FROM bank_transactions
  GROUP BY strftime('%Y-%m', date)
),
c AS (SELECT fy, fy_month_idx, SUM(net) OVER (PARTITION BY fy ORDER BY fy_month_idx) AS cum_net FROM m),
cur AS (SELECT MAX(fy) AS fy FROM m),
months(idx, label) AS (VALUES (0,'Jul'),(1,'Aug'),(2,'Sep'),(3,'Oct'),(4,'Nov'),(5,'Dec'),(6,'Jan'),(7,'Feb'),(8,'Mar'),(9,'Apr'),(10,'May'),(11,'Jun'))
SELECT months.label AS fy_month,
       (SELECT c.cum_net FROM c, cur WHERE c.fy = cur.fy     AND c.fy_month_idx = months.idx) AS this_fy,
       (SELECT c.cum_net FROM c, cur WHERE c.fy = cur.fy - 1 AND c.fy_month_idx = months.idx) AS last_fy
FROM months
ORDER BY months.idx
notes: The financial year laid out July to June, running total of net cash, current FY against the one before. Written relative to the latest FY in the data, so it rolls over on 1 July with no edits. The bank file starts in August 2025, so last FY has no July point.

title: Who owes what
query:
SELECT i.client,
       SUM(i.balance_aud) AS owed,
       SUM(CASE WHEN i.days_past_due > 0 THEN i.balance_aud ELSE 0 END) AS overdue,
       COUNT(*) AS open_invoices,
       MAX(i.days_past_due) AS oldest_days_past_due,
       (SELECT x.next_chase_step FROM invoices x
         WHERE x.client = i.client AND x.balance_aud > 0
         ORDER BY x.days_past_due DESC LIMIT 1) AS next_chase_step
FROM invoices i
WHERE i.balance_aud > 0
GROUP BY i.client
ORDER BY owed DESC
notes: A table, because the next action is words, not a quantity. The chase step shown is the one on the client's oldest open invoice, which is the step that matters first. The in-cell bar keeps the ranking readable without a second chart.

title: Payment habits
query:
WITH pay AS (
  SELECT i.client, i.invoice_no, i.issue_date, i.due_date, b.date AS paid_date, b.credit_in AS paid,
         julianday(b.date) - julianday(i.issue_date) AS days_to_pay,
         julianday(b.date) - julianday(i.due_date)   AS days_late
  FROM bank_transactions b
  JOIN invoices i ON i.invoice_no = substr(b.description, instr(b.description, 'INV-'))
  WHERE b.credit_in IS NOT NULL
),
p AS (SELECT client, AVG(days_late) AS avg_days_late, SUM(days_late > 0) AS late_payments, COUNT(*) AS payments FROM pay GROUP BY client),
i AS (SELECT client, SUM(amount_aud) AS billed, SUM(balance_aud) AS outstanding FROM invoices GROUP BY client)
SELECT i.client,
       ROUND(p.avg_days_late, 1) AS avg_days_late,
       i.billed, i.outstanding, p.late_payments, p.payments,
       ROUND(100.0 * sqrt(i.outstanding / (SELECT MAX(outstanding) FROM i)), 1) AS bubble
FROM i JOIN p USING (client)
ORDER BY i.outstanding DESC

label.formatter: a full 14-day term late or more

notes: Each client placed by how late their payments land (x) against how much we bill them (y); bubble area is what they still owe, scaled in SQL (sqrt of share of the largest) so the visualMap range stays static JSON. The three status series are filter transforms over the one injected dataset, which also lets each group put its labels on the side with room. Top right is the danger corner: big, late, and still owing.

title: Where invoiced money went

queries.links:
WITH pay AS (
  SELECT i.client, i.invoice_no, i.issue_date, i.due_date, b.date AS paid_date, b.credit_in AS paid,
         julianday(b.date) - julianday(i.issue_date) AS days_to_pay,
         julianday(b.date) - julianday(i.due_date)   AS days_late
  FROM bank_transactions b
  JOIN invoices i ON i.invoice_no = substr(b.description, instr(b.description, 'INV-'))
  WHERE b.credit_in IS NOT NULL
),
flow(source, target, value) AS (
  SELECT 'Invoiced', 'Paid on time', (SELECT SUM(paid) FROM pay WHERE days_late <= 0)
  UNION ALL SELECT 'Invoiced', 'Paid late', (SELECT SUM(paid) FROM pay WHERE days_late > 0)
  UNION ALL SELECT 'Invoiced', 'Still outstanding', (SELECT SUM(balance_aud) FROM invoices)
  UNION ALL SELECT 'Paid late', '1-30 days late',  (SELECT SUM(paid) FROM pay WHERE days_late BETWEEN 1 AND 30)
  UNION ALL SELECT 'Paid late', '31-60 days late', (SELECT SUM(paid) FROM pay WHERE days_late BETWEEN 31 AND 60)
  UNION ALL SELECT 'Paid late', '61+ days late',   (SELECT SUM(paid) FROM pay WHERE days_late > 60)
  UNION ALL SELECT 'Still outstanding', 'Not yet due',     (SELECT SUM(balance_aud) FROM invoices WHERE ageing_bucket = 'current')
  UNION ALL SELECT 'Still outstanding', 'Overdue 1-30',    (SELECT SUM(balance_aud) FROM invoices WHERE ageing_bucket = '1-30')
  UNION ALL SELECT 'Still outstanding', 'Overdue 31-60',   (SELECT SUM(balance_aud) FROM invoices WHERE ageing_bucket = '31-60')
  UNION ALL SELECT 'Still outstanding', 'Overdue 61-90',   (SELECT SUM(balance_aud) FROM invoices WHERE ageing_bucket = '61-90')
  UNION ALL SELECT 'Still outstanding', 'Overdue 90+',     (SELECT SUM(balance_aud) FROM invoices WHERE ageing_bucket = '90+')
)
SELECT source, target, value FROM flow WHERE value > 0
queries.nodes:
WITH pay AS (
  SELECT i.client, i.invoice_no, i.issue_date, i.due_date, b.date AS paid_date, b.credit_in AS paid,

  FROM bank_transactions b

  WHERE b.credit_in IS NOT NULL
),
n(name, color, value) AS (
  SELECT 'Invoiced', 'var(--chart-1)', (SELECT SUM(amount_aud) FROM invoices)
  UNION ALL SELECT 'Paid on time', 'var(--good)', (SELECT SUM(paid) FROM pay WHERE days_late <= 0)
  UNION ALL SELECT 'Paid late', 'var(--warning)', (SELECT SUM(paid) FROM pay WHERE days_late > 0)
  UNION ALL SELECT 'Still outstanding', 'var(--neutral)', (SELECT SUM(balance_aud) FROM invoices)
  UNION ALL SELECT '1-30 days late', 'var(--age-1-30)', (SELECT SUM(paid) FROM pay WHERE days_late BETWEEN 1 AND 30)
  UNION ALL SELECT '31-60 days late', 'var(--age-31-60)', (SELECT SUM(paid) FROM pay WHERE days_late BETWEEN 31 AND 60)
  UNION ALL SELECT '61+ days late', 'var(--age-61-90)', (SELECT SUM(paid) FROM pay WHERE days_late > 60)
  UNION ALL SELECT 'Not yet due', 'var(--age-current)', (SELECT SUM(balance_aud) FROM invoices WHERE ageing_bucket = 'current')
  UNION ALL SELECT 'Overdue 1-30', 'var(--age-1-30)', (SELECT SUM(balance_aud) FROM invoices WHERE ageing_bucket = '1-30')
  UNION ALL SELECT 'Overdue 31-60', 'var(--age-31-60)', (SELECT SUM(balance_aud) FROM invoices WHERE ageing_bucket = '31-60')
  UNION ALL SELECT 'Overdue 61-90', 'var(--age-61-90)', (SELECT SUM(balance_aud) FROM invoices WHERE ageing_bucket = '61-90')
  UNION ALL SELECT 'Overdue 90+', 'var(--age-90-plus)', (SELECT SUM(balance_aud) FROM invoices WHERE ageing_bucket = '90+')
)
SELECT name, color AS "itemStyle.color" FROM n WHERE value > 0

notes: Every invoiced dollar traced to where it ended up: paid on or before the due date, paid late (and how late), or still owed (and how old). Sankey ignores dataset, so the recipe uses two named queries bound to series.0.links and series.0.data; a column aliased "itemStyle.color" becomes a nested key. The three first-level amounts add up to total invoiced exactly.

title: Days late, by client and month invoiced
query:
WITH pay AS (
  SELECT i.client, i.invoice_no, i.issue_date, i.due_date, b.date AS paid_date, b.credit_in AS paid,
         julianday(b.date) - julianday(i.issue_date) AS days_to_pay,
         julianday(b.date) - julianday(i.due_date)   AS days_late
  FROM bank_transactions b
  JOIN invoices i ON i.invoice_no = substr(b.description, instr(b.description, 'INV-'))
  WHERE b.credit_in IS NOT NULL
),
months AS (SELECT DISTINCT strftime('%Y-%m', issue_date) AS ym FROM invoices),
clients AS (SELECT client, AVG(days_late) AS overall FROM pay GROUP BY client),
cell AS (SELECT client, strftime('%Y-%m', issue_date) AS ym, ROUND(AVG(days_late), 1) AS avg_days_late, COUNT(*) AS payments FROM pay GROUP BY 1, 2)
SELECT substr('JanFebMarAprMayJunJulAugSepOctNovDec', (CAST(strftime('%m', months.ym || '-01') AS INTEGER) - 1) * 3 + 1, 3) || ' ' || substr(months.ym, 3, 2) AS month,
       clients.client, cell.avg_days_late, cell.payments
FROM months CROSS JOIN clients
LEFT JOIN cell ON cell.ym = months.ym AND cell.client = clients.client
ORDER BY months.ym, clients.overall
notes: The scatter says who pays late; this says whether it is a habit or a one-off. Diverging scale with a neutral midpoint at the due date, clamped at ±45 days so one very late payment does not wash out the rest. Rows are sorted by overall lateness, so the chronic payers sit together at the top. Blank cells are months with no paid invoice.

title: Where the money goes
query:
SELECT description AS category,
       SUM(debit_out) AS spent,
       COUNT(*) AS payments,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM(debit_out) / (SELECT SUM(debit_out) FROM bank_transactions), 1) AS pct_of_spend
FROM bank_transactions
WHERE debit_out IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY description
ORDER BY spent DESC
notes: Debits grouped by their bank description, sorted. One colour, because the categories have no order and length already carries the value. Rent and supplies are the fixed base; BAS is the lumpy one that explains the quarterly dips in cash flow.

title: How payments were matched
query:
SELECT match_method,
       COUNT(*) AS invoices,
       SUM(paid_aud) AS matched_aud,
       CASE WHEN match_method LIKE 'manual%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS needs_human
FROM invoices
WHERE match_method IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY match_method
ORDER BY invoices DESC
notes: How the money clerk tied each bank credit to its invoice. Emphasis, not a rainbow: the one bar that still needs the owner is coloured, the rest are muted. A rejected donut: four near-equal slices are hard to compare.

title: Work by agent and status
query:
SELECT assignee,
       SUM(status = 'backlog')     AS backlog,
       SUM(status = 'todo')        AS todo,
       SUM(status = 'in_progress') AS in_progress,
       SUM(status = 'in_review')   AS in_review,
       SUM(status = 'blocked')     AS blocked,
       SUM(status = 'done')        AS done,
       COUNT(*)                    AS total
FROM tasks
GROUP BY assignee
ORDER BY total DESC
notes: One bar per agent, stacked in pipeline order with blocked at the outer end where it is easiest to spot. Done and blocked take the status colours; the working states take series colours.

title: Throughput by week
query:
WITH RECURSIVE wk(week_start) AS (
  SELECT date(MIN(created_at), '-6 days', 'weekday 1') FROM tasks
  UNION ALL
  SELECT date(week_start, '+7 days') FROM wk
  WHERE date(week_start, '+7 days') <= (SELECT MAX(created_at) FROM tasks)
)
SELECT CAST(strftime('%d', week_start) AS INTEGER) || ' ' || substr('JanFebMarAprMayJunJulAugSepOctNovDec', (CAST(strftime('%m', week_start) AS INTEGER) - 1) * 3 + 1, 3) AS week,
       week_start,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tasks WHERE created_at   >= week_start AND created_at   < date(week_start, '+7 days')) AS created,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tasks WHERE completed_at >= week_start AND completed_at < date(week_start, '+7 days')) AS completed,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tasks WHERE created_at < date(week_start, '+7 days')
          AND (completed_at IS NULL OR completed_at >= date(week_start, '+7 days'))) AS open_at_week_end
FROM wk
ORDER BY week_start
notes: Weeks from a recursive spine (Monday start) so a quiet week still shows as zero. Created against completed, with the open pile as a line on the same count axis. If the line keeps climbing, agents are being handed work faster than they finish it.

title: Agents, work and clients

queries.nodes:
SELECT name, category, symbolSize, value, tip AS "tooltip.formatter" FROM (
  SELECT assignee AS name, 0 AS category, 16 + 2 * COUNT(*) AS symbolSize, COUNT(*) AS value,
         assignee || ': ' || COUNT(*) || ' tasks' AS tip, -COUNT(*) AS ord
  FROM tasks GROUP BY assignee
  UNION ALL
  SELECT title, 1, 8 + 2 * COUNT(*), COUNT(*),
         title || ': ' || COUNT(*) || ' tasks',
         CASE WHEN title = 'Chase invoices over 30 days' THEN 1000 ELSE -COUNT(*) END
  FROM tasks GROUP BY title
  UNION ALL
  SELECT client, 2,
         ROUND(10 + 26 * sqrt(SUM(balance_aud) / (SELECT MAX(o) FROM (SELECT SUM(balance_aud) AS o FROM invoices WHERE days_past_due > 30 GROUP BY client)))),
         SUM(balance_aud),
         client || ': ' || printf('A$%,d', SUM(balance_aud)) || ' more than 30 days overdue',
         -SUM(balance_aud)
  FROM invoices WHERE days_past_due > 30 AND balance_aud > 0 GROUP BY client
)
ORDER BY category, ord, name
queries.links:
SELECT assignee AS source, title AS target, COUNT(*) AS value, 0.5 + COUNT(*) AS "lineStyle.width", 'solid' AS "lineStyle.type" FROM tasks GROUP BY assignee, title
UNION ALL
SELECT 'Chase invoices over 30 days', client, SUM(balance_aud), 1.5, 'dashed'
FROM invoices WHERE days_past_due > 30 AND balance_aud > 0 GROUP BY client

notes: Agents, task types and overdue clients sit on one circle in that order, placed by SQL ORDER BY, so the picture is the same on every load. Agents link to the kinds of task they hold (line weight = how many). The tasks table has no client or invoice column, so the only client link drawn is an inferred one, shown dashed: the task type "Chase invoices over 30 days" to every client with a balance more than 30 days overdue. Add client or invoice_no to tasks and the second half of the links query becomes a real join.
